# Parley v0.1.64

This unnotarized test beta adds a Stop item to every agent pane's menu, lets
a merged team worktree be removed in one step, and makes the sidebar's
disclosure arrows easy to hit. It also fixes a workspace layout that could
be lost silently after many saved layouts.

## No restart needed

The agent protocol is unchanged at version 33. Panes started under v0.1.63
keep working after the update.

## Stop a pane without closing it

- A started agent pane's menu (the header's ellipsis and the sidebar's
  right-click) now offers **Stop…**, beside Restart. It asks first, ends the
  vendor's process and keeps the pane as a stopped placeholder that you can
  start or resume later from the same menu.
- For a container pane, Stop first stops and removes its container. The
  pane's saved vendor login and conversations stay in its volume. Until now,
  the only way to stop a container pane without closing it was Status Center
  › Health › Containers.
- Moving a container pane while its container was being stopped, by Close,
  Stop or closing a workspace, could remove the container and then refuse,
  leaving the pane running. A pane being stopped or closed now refuses a
  move until that finishes.

## Removing a merged team worktree

- After a merge request was merged with its source branch deleted, removing
  its worktree from the Worktrees window was refused with "Git status could
  not be read". The real cause was the branch's upstream, which no longer
  existed. When Git reports the upstream gone, or cannot read it, and the
  primary checkout already contains the tree's commits, the tree can now be
  removed. Otherwise the refusal names the upstream. The board reads
  "upstream gone" instead of "push state unknown".
- A folder marked as a cache by a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file, such as Swift's
  `.build`, is no longer searched for repositories. Its package clones made
  every Swift worktree unremovable. The removal confirmation names each such
  folder and says it was not inspected, and that everything in it is
  deleted, including any repository or local change.
- A real Git repository hidden in an ignored folder is refused as "an
  independent Git repository". It used to be misnamed as another registered
  worktree.

## Easier to click

- The sidebar's disclosure arrows, and every plain button in the main view,
  now respond across their whole area rather than only where they are drawn.
  Opening or closing a section no longer takes several attempts.
- On macOS 27, a double-click in the middle of the main window's empty title
  bar, where the window keeps its hidden title, now does what Desktop & Dock
  settings say
  (zoom or minimise). A text field in the title bar still keeps its own
  clicks.

## Other fixes

- After many saved layouts had replaced workspaces, a new workspace could
  silently lose its pane layout, because the record of each replaced
  workspace was never removed. Replaced workspaces are now forgotten, and a
  full record store makes room from the longest-unused closed workspace.
- Help covers container panes more fully: signing in for every vendor, how
  a pane picks up a rebuilt or different image (each start checks the image
  again), and that a pane's login belongs to the pane, not the image.

## For people building container images

- `docs/container-images.md` is now the one guide for container panes:
  - building an image;
  - using and changing an image for a pane;
  - signing in to each vendor;
  - reaching a service on your Mac, and what that opens;
  - known limits.
- `docs/parley-agents-fetch.sh` fetches the Linux builds of all four vendors
  and checks each against its publisher's checksum.
  `docs/parley-agents.Dockerfile` builds them into one image, with the Prax
  CLI. Each pane still runs in its own container.

## Validation and known limits

The release workflow repeats the deterministic checks, the repository scans,
the app build, the 25-round Ghostty soak, packaging, checksums and
packaged-launch verification before publishing this beta. The public scan now
streams Git history, so it no longer has a size limit.

Checked in code and automated checks, but not yet by hand in the app:
- Stop… on a host pane and on a container pane, and starting it again;
- removing a merged team worktree that holds a Swift build cache;
- the sidebar's disclosure arrows and the title-bar double-click;
- the v0.1.63 sidebar items and the v0.1.62 items still waiting for a hand
  test.

This is an ad-hoc-signed, unnotarized test beta. It does not update the
stable Sparkle feed or Homebrew cask. Follow the included installation
instructions.
